findingDetails.title: Commit-Id gates accept the reserved all-zero ordinal
findingDetails.case: In a repository with skilled.commitId=true and no prior zero-valued id, a message containing Commit-Id: 0000000 passes the seven-digit message checks, and a pushed commit carrying it passes the pre-push presence gate.
findingDetails.evidence: The shared policy helper accepts any seven digits; the message-contract pattern is ^[0-9]{7}$ and its validator applies that pattern; pre-push Gate 7 uses the same shape. The allocator constrains ids to 0000001..9999999 and its test rejects 0000000.
findingDetails.userImpact: An ID-enforced repository can store and push an ordinal its own allocator declares invalid, leaving history outside the sequence contract.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The hook helper and pre-push gate use seven-digit-only checks, while the allocator is stricter. Existing commit-msg coverage tests a short malformed value but not zero; the push test exercises a positive value only.
findingDetails.recommendation: Apply one positive-ordinal validator at both commit and push boundaries, and add an all-zero rejection case to the hook tests.
findingDetails.claim: The Commit-Id message and push gates reject every value the allocator considers invalid.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked both hook acceptance paths, the configured message pattern, allocator invariant, and nearby tests for a zero exception or lower-bound check; none appears downstream.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The gates may rely on the normal stamper to produce valid IDs. That does not cover manual message edits or commits created without hooks, which the commit and push validators are intended to catch.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Verified evidence that a shared validation step rejects 0000000 before commit and push, or that the allocator contract changes to accept zero.
